screens.prompt: In B7, add up the months that went up and leave the drops alone.

hints.syntax: =SUMIF(B2:B6,">0"): the condition is a comparison, written in quotes.
hints.func-sumif: SUM takes everything. You want the months that went up and nothing else.
hints.require-ref: Test the changes from the grid, not from numbers typed into the formula.
hints.value: The gains are 12, 15 and 20, which total 47.
hints.error: A comparison without quotes around it is read as a cell reference, so the answer comes back wrong rather than broken.

reject.why: 36 — the gains and the drops netted off against each other
-11, the losses rather than the gains
the range starts on row 3, so January's 12 is never tested
division by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!
the missing comma leaves one argument where two are needed

screens.prompt: In B7, report the size of the losses as a positive number.

hints.syntax: =-SUMIF(B2:B6,"<0"): the minus sign turns a negative total into a positive size.
hints.func-sumif: Add only the negative weeks, and let SUMIF do the adding.
hints.require-ref: Read the variances from the grid so the filter applies to real cells.
hints.value: The losses add to -15, so their size is 15.
hints.error: The minus belongs in front of the function, not inside the condition. ">-0" matches nothing and returns 0.

reject.why: -6, which nets the good weeks against the bad ones
-15: the right rows, but reported with the sign on
9 — the winning weeks instead of the losing ones
the range starts on row 3, so the first loss is missed
division by zero, so the cell holds #DIV/0!
the missing comma leaves one argument where two are needed

docs.explain:
A plain SUM over a profit-and-loss column returns the net, which is the least informative figure in it. SUMIF splits the column by sign instead: ">0" keeps the gains and "<0" keeps the drops.

Zero belongs to neither bucket, so a flat month vanishes from both totals and the pair will not add back to the net. A net that misses the column by one month's figure is that missing zero.

The second screen puts a minus in front of the function so the losses read as a size rather than a negative. The minus does not change which rows matched, so a wrong condition still shows up as the wrong size.

errors.text: The criteria range holds text that cannot be compared with a number, or a comparison lost its quotes and is read as a cell reference.
The function is misspelled, or SUMIFS was used with the argument order SUMIF keeps.
Losses are negative, so a report that wants their size needs the minus in front of SUMIF. Without it the figure reads as -15 rather than 15.

docs.atWork: A monthly variance report that shows total gains and total losses on separate lines.
docs.outcome: Total the positive and negative rows separately instead of netting a column.
docs.teaches: SUMIF with a sign comparison, and flipping a negative total

seo.title: Add only the positive or negative rows
seo.description: Splitting a profit column by sign with SUMIF gives the two numbers a report wants: what was gained and what was lost. A zero month counts in neither.
